topic.label: Classics
topic.desc: Classics: the languages, literature, history, philosophy and material culture of ancient Greece and Rome.

concepts: Grammar, syntax and vocabulary of Attic, Homeric and Koine Greek as the basis for reading original texts.
Grammar, syntax and style of classical and post-classical Latin prose and verse.
Epic, drama, lyric, history and oratory read in their genres, traditions and reception.
Political, social and economic history of the Greek and Roman world from the Bronze Age to late antiquity.
Material remains of Greek and Roman sites, architecture, sculpture, pottery and coins.
Presocratic, Platonic, Aristotelian, Stoic and Epicurean thought in ethics, metaphysics and logic.
Reading, restoring and dating inscriptions and papyri as primary documentary evidence.
skills: Parses each Greek word for lemma, case, tense, mood and voice and checks the analysis against standard grammars.
Produces a literal and a readable translation of a Greek passage and checks every clause against the parsed original.
Identifies declension, conjugation and syntactic function for each Latin word and verifies agreement across the sentence.
Renders English sentences into idiomatic classical Latin and checks grammar and word choice against attested usage.
Writes a close reading of a passage that ties diction, imagery and structure to genre, with every claim tied to a line reference.
Scans hexameter, elegiac and lyric lines into long and short syllables and flags lines that do not fit the meter.
Traces how a classical text was read and adapted in later periods and checks each claimed adaptation against a cited source.
Assesses the reliability, bias and date of an ancient historical source and compares its account with independent evidence.
Builds a dated timeline of events, rulers and magistracies and reconciles conflicting dating systems.
Dates pottery, coins and sculpture by style, context and stratigraphy and states the evidence for each date range.
Interprets the plan and phases of an excavated site and checks the reading against published excavation reports.
Reconstructs an argument from an ancient philosophical text as numbered premises and conclusion and checks validity and textual fidelity.
Compares positions of two schools on one question and checks each attribution against primary passages.
Transcribes and expands abbreviations in an inscription using standard editorial signs and checks restorations against parallels.
Produces a diplomatic and normalised text of a papyrus fragment and records every uncertain reading.
